newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Novolipetsk investors rights rulings postponed.
newsitem.headline: Novolipetsk investors rights rulings postponed.

text.p: Rulings on prominent shareholders' rights cases brought against Russian steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine have been postponed, a judge involved in the case said on Thursday.

A spokesman for one of the plaintiffs said hearings were held on Wednesday in cases involving the Sputnik fund, an investment arm of Renaissance Capital, and Bank MFK, which is associated with Uneximbank (Russian Oneksimbank).
He said a hearing of the case brought by U.S. investment fund Cambridge Capital Management, which owns 17.2 percent of Novolipetsk shares, was scheduled for April 23.
Representatives of Sputnik, which owns nine percent of Novolipetsk shares, and MFK, which owns 15 percent, were unavailable for comment on Thursday.

Sputnik and Cambridge claim management refused to consider its nominees to the board of directors and MFK, whose case is being handled by the State Property Committee, says the factory stripped it of its shareholder voting rights last year.
The Federal Securities Commission is also investigating the company.
Senior Novolipetsk managers could not be reached for comment on Thursday, but have said they acted in accordance with company rules.

The judge, who asked that he not be named, said rulings on the cases had been postponed after some sides were granted permission to file further evidence. He did not say when the next hearings would be held.

Novolipetsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat (NLMK) is also planning to buy back a 37.5 percent block of shares owned by a group of shareholders which includes the Trans-World metals trading company, Trans-World Group said.
